summary: The loop-side backstop. When a session returns 0, wrote no verdict this iteration, and left changes in the tree, the loop now re-invokes it once asking for a verdict before falling through to its existing exit 1. Gated on a dirty tree and on no pending commit retry, bounded to one attempt per iteration, and it shares has_verdict_artifact() with the Stop hook's exported vocabulary so the two cannot disagree about what an ending is.
suggested_commit_message: session lifetime: one retry when a session leaves work unclaimed
reviewer_notes: Deliberately a backstop, not the primary fix. It fires after the process died, so anything backgrounded is already gone — which is why the retry PROMPT says so explicitly and tells the session not to wait for or restart it. The hook prevents the loss; this handles what the hook cannot see (crash, external kill, missing or failing hook). The kickoff asked for the retry to be proven with the hook absent, and the loop harness is exactly that: a stub run-phase.sh with no claude and no hooks.

The first gate was too broad and two existing regression tests caught it — v0.6.0's verify-retry and v0.6.3's stranded-approval. Both set PENDING_COMMIT_RETRY, which is a dirty tree the loop ALREADY resolves at this same boundary by committing the approval under its own phase's message. Prodding there spends a turn asking for a verdict that exists. Added `[[ -z "$PENDING_COMMIT_RETRY" ]]` and a dedicated pin so the narrowing is deliberate rather than incidental.

The retry prompt leads with phase-update.json and says why (commits the work AND the loop continues). That was the move available to all three failed sessions in the incident and none of them took it.
Verified it does NOT fire on a clean tree with no artifact: a legitimately empty iteration has nothing to claim, and nudging it would only burn a turn.
